title: A tale of two Nvidias
lede: On TechCrunch's Equity podcast, three reporters set Nvidia's strong earnings against a public push, backed by Elon Musk and others, to bring back former CEO Jensen Huang.

points: Nvidia reported soaring revenue, beat expectations and gave strong guidance, yet its share price has been falling.
Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will stop selling H200 chips in China, as the Trump administration moves to shut remote access through data centers in places like Malaysia.
Critics of Nvidia's China stance estimate about 20% of its business reaches China indirectly, so the cutoff could hurt.
Musk and others circulated a petition for Huang's return and Huang says he is ready; the company says it is not happening.
The hosts call a return unlikely while an investigation into alleged secret chip sales to China is open, and expect the board to protect its control.

sections.text: Closing the remote-access route through data centers outside China narrows who can rent Nvidia's top chips, while the leadership fight adds uncertainty at the main supplier of AI compute.
